haiku-low.q1: It does not differ. Both return HTTP 401, the login page with "Invalid email or password", and no cookie. An app-side bcrypt check runs for unknown emails too.
haiku-low.q2: The attempt is refused with HTTP 429 and Retry-After, without checking the password. The email is locked for 15 minutes.
haiku-low.q3: After the password check passes, the old session the cookie pointed to is deleted, and a brand-new random session ID is issued.
haiku-low.q4: Only the opaque 43-character session ID; no user data. The cookie is flagged HttpOnly, so page scripts should not read it.
haiku-low.q5: It stops at 12 hours after login, even with constant activity. The 30-minute idle limit restarts on each request, but the 12-hour cap is absolute.
haiku-low.q6: It deletes nothing extra, clears the cookie with Set-Cookie, and redirects with 302 to /login. The login page gives no reason.
haiku-low.q7: The server deletes the session record before replying, then clears the cookie and redirects to /login. If no session exists, the result is the same with no error.
haiku-low.q8: In one shared Redis instance used by both app instances. Each instance reads the session by the SHA-256 hash of the session ID key.
haiku-low.q9: In a Redis sorted set keyed by the email hash, one entry per attempt scored by Redis time in ms. Entries older than 10 minutes are dropped.
haiku-low.q10: It checks the session exists and that now is before abs_expires_at. It then sets the Redis TTL to min(1800 s, abs_expires_at minus now).
haiku-low.q11: HTTP 503 with a generic "Sign-in is temporarily unavailable" page and no cookie. The user can retry, and the old session is deleted only where that step succeeded.
haiku-low.q12: Redis key expiry does it: the 30-minute idle TTL, capped by the 12-hour absolute limit. The design has no sweeper job.

sonnet.q1: It doesn't differ: both get HTTP 401 with the same login page and "Invalid email or password" message, no cookie. (The app also runs a dummy bcrypt compare for unknown emails so timing matches.)
sonnet.q2: It gets HTTP 429 with the login page message "Too many sign-in attempts. Please try again later." and Retry-After set to the lock's remaining seconds (900 if the lock just started). The password is not checked, and a 15-minute lock is set. This is the 6th attempt: the first 5 pass the gate.
sonnet.q3: After a successful password check, the app creates a brand-new random session and deletes the old session (DEL in Redis) if the cookie looked valid (43 base64url chars). If that delete fails, it returns 503. The login never succeeds with the old session left alive.
sonnet.q4: Only an opaque random session ID (43-char base64url), with no user data. The cookie is HttpOnly, so page scripts cannot read it. It is also Secure and SameSite=Lax.
sonnet.q5: At 12 hours after login, the absolute limit, even if they are continuously active. Each request restarts the 30-minute idle clock, but the TTL is clamped to the absolute deadline.
sonnet.q6: CHECK returns MISSING. The server sends a Set-Cookie that clears the cookie and a 302 redirect to /login, with no explanation shown. (If the 12-hour limit was hit, the session is also deleted.)
sonnet.q7: If a valid-looking cookie was sent, the server runs DEL on the session record in Redis before replying. Deleting a missing key is not an error. The reply is always the cookie-clearing Set-Cookie plus 302 /login, with or without a session. If Redis errors, it returns 503 and keeps the cookie.
sonnet.q8: In one Redis instance shared by both app instances. Any instance looks it up by the SHA-256 hash of the cookie's session ID (key sess:{hash}) via the CHECK Lua script, so no sticky sessions are needed.
sonnet.q9: In Redis, in the sorted set lf:{sha256(email)}. Each attempt is a member (a random nonce) with the Redis time in ms as its score. The GATE script drops entries older than 10 minutes, by score, before counting.
sonnet.q10: The CHECK script, on the Redis clock, checks that sess:{hash} exists and that now is less than abs_expires_at (created_at + 12 h). The idle limit is enforced by the Redis TTL. When valid, it resets the TTL to min(1800 s, abs_expires_at - now) and returns the user_id.
sonnet.q11: A 503 response showing the login page with the message "Sign-in is temporarily unavailable. Please try again in a few minutes." and the email kept. No cookie is set, and the user can retry.
sonnet.q12: Redis TTL expiry removes them. There is no sweeper job.
